name: Unverferth Manufacturing Co., Inc.
old_description: Our Delphos facility is located in Northwest Ohio and is the founding home of the Killbros brand. Purchased by Unverferth in 1993, this facility specializes in producing key components and assemblies for multiple product lines, including seed tenders, ATV sprayers, header transports and smaller grain carts. With a strong focus on precision machining, welding, and fabrication, the Delphos location manufacturers some of the highest quality agricultural machinery in the industry.
about:
Unverferth Manufacturing Co., Inc. began in 1948 when Lawrence G. and Richard Unverferth launched L.G. Unverferth Manufacturing in Kalida, Ohio, with a family loan secured by war bonds. Their first products were combine shucker levers and a patented bolt‑on dual‑wheel extension that founded the company’s wheel‑system business. The firm remains family‑owned; its corporate headquarters are now in Casselton, North Dakota, while the Kalida campus handles design, engineering, fabrication, welding, powder coating and assembly.

Eight sales and distribution branches in the U.S. and Canada support the six brands.

Blu‑Jet focuses on anhydrous ammonia and liquid fertilizer application; Brent leads high‑capacity grain carts; Orthman supplies strip‑till and toolbar systems; Top Air builds pull‑type and self‑propelled sprayers with T‑Tank and steerable‑hitch technology; and the Unverferth brand covers wheel systems, seed handling and tillage.

name: Urschel Laboratories Inc
old_description: Urschel is the world’s leading manufacturer of industrial food cutting machines, helping processors across the globe achieve precise, high-volume results. Our equipment is engineered to handle nearly any product — from fruits, vegetables, and potatoes to meat, cheese, baked goods, comitrol processing, and pet food. Whether you need perfect slices, uniform dices, fine purees, or controlled granulation, Urschel delivers reliable performance and unmatched quality.
about:
Urschel Laboratories was founded in 1910 in Valparaiso, Indiana, by William E. Urschel, who invented the Gooseberry Snipper to automate a labor-intensive hand process. The company relocated to Chesterton, Indiana, and remained a privately held family business for four generations until March 3, 2016, when the Urschel family sold the company to its employees through an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP), making it 100 percent employee-owned. Patrick Urschel serves as CEO.

The company designs and manufactures industrial food cutting machines, including dicers, slicers, shredders, and milling equipment. Its product line performs slicing, dicing, strip cutting, shredding, granulating, milling, and pureeing for high-volume food processors. Current models include the Little Gem Aspire™ Dicer, M VersaPro® Dicer, DiversaCut 2110A® Dicer, Sprint 2® Dicer, and several Affinity® series dicers. Urschel also distributes KRONEN commercial processing systems in the U.S., Mexico, Pakistan, China, Italy, and across Asia.

Urschel serves the food processing and allied industries, supplying equipment to processors of fruits, vegetables, potatoes, meat, cheese, baked goods, nut products, and pet food. The company reports a presence in more than 130 countries.

Urschel attributes its differentiation to its in-house Innovation & Development team, which develops patented cutting technologies through extensive R&D, and to its employee-ownership culture, which the company says aligns every team member with long-term customer success.

name: Uzelac Industries Inc.
old_description: Uzelac Industries was founded in 2003 by Michael Uzelac following the acquisition of Poja Sheetmetal, and later Duske Engineering in 2006. Drawing on decades of experience in manufacturing leadership, Michael launched the company with a focus on contract fabrication, which evolved into a specialized operation designing and manufacturing direct-fired rotary dryers.
about:
Uzelac Industries was founded in 2003 by Michael Uzelac in Greendale, Wisconsin, after he acquired Poja Sheetmetal (established 1956) and later Duske Engineering (established 1980).

The company designs and manufactures custom direct-fired rotary drying systems, each engineered to a customer’s specific process requirements. In addition to its core dryer line, Uzelac provides contract fabrication for large equipment OEMs, offering brake bending, rolling, shearing, punching, MIG/TIG welding, and waterjet cutting from a plant equipped with 25-ton and 10-ton crane bays. Its workforce consists of journeyman fabricators and engineers with 40-plus years of experience, and the firm holds several U.S. patents on dryer design.

Uzelac serves the hemp, poultry, biomass, rendering, biosolids, and gasification sectors. In poultry, it has supplied rotary dryers to Herbruck’s Poultry Ranch, Michael Foods, Foster Farms, and Tyson for over 30 years. Its systems also support anaerobic digestion and bioenergy projects worldwide, with installations across multiple countries.

The business was built on the shared values of integrity, customer satisfaction, and innovation inherited from Industrial MetalFab Specialties and Duske Drying Systems. Michael Uzelac’s vision combined the craftsmanship of Poja Sheetmetal with Duske’s custom engineering to create a specialist in direct-fired rotary technology, a focus that remains central to the company’s identity today.

name: VESCO-NM
old_description: VESCO-NM manufactures state of the art proprietary Molecular Beam Epitaxy (MBE) systems and components as well as components for Metal Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition (MOCVD) systems. We specialize in MBE, MOCVD and semiconductor cleanroom tools decommissioning, decontamination and installations.
about:
VESCO-NM is based in Albuquerque, New Mexico. The company was founded in 2009 by Dr. Abdel-Rahman El-Emawy, who earned his Ph.D. from Colorado State University in 1996 with a dissertation on II/VI material growth by MBE. After joining the Center for High Technology Materials at the University of New Mexico as a research professor, he led MBE and MOCVD programs for quantum dots, dilute nitrides, and spintronic materials. His earlier career included work as an aircraft avionics engineer and development of GaAs-based BiFETs for telecommunications. Dr. El-Emawy founded VESCO-NM to commercialize his expertise in epitaxial growth equipment.

The company designs and manufactures proprietary molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) systems—such as the Ultima 310—and a range of MBE components including valved crackers, effusion cells, RF plasma sources, and tantalum-wire heaters. It also produces components for metal organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) systems. In addition to new equipment, VESCO-NM provides decommissioning, decontamination, refurbishment, and installation services for semiconductor cleanroom tools worldwide. Its Albuquerque facility houses a machine shop with CNC milling, CNC turning, wire EDM, water jet cutting, and welding stations, plus a cleanroom for assembly and testing and CAD workstations for design and simulation.

VESCO-NM serves research institutions, universities, private industry, and government agencies across the globe. Its equipment supports applications in crystal growth, material deposition, LED manufacturing, renewable energy, thin-film technologies, and consumer electronics. The company reports more than 300 customers served worldwide.

The firm emphasizes four core values: quality in design and fabrication, value through reasonable pricing, customer service, and on-time delivery. It differentiates itself with proprietary source designs that achieve high flux uniformity, stability, and dissociation efficiency, all manufactured in-house under controlled conditions.

Its Hyde Park shop produces floating and wood-framed staircases, steel- and wood-framed decks, stainless-steel cable railings, spiral staircases, and ADA-compliant commercial railings. Every component is hand-crafted from high-grade stainless steel by a team whose combined experience exceeds 60 years, and the firm has completed more than 400 projects to date. Optional LED lighting, including cascading LEDs for monorail stairs and handrail-integrated LEDs, is available for architectural upgrades.

Clients range from individual homeowners building lakefront retreats or mountain lodges to architects and builders specifying commercial and ADA railings. The company's turnkey packages cover in-home consultation, custom design and fabrication, clean structural installation, and a final safety inspection with ongoing support.

Lambert started the business to combine heavy-duty engineering with clean, modern lines, delivering rock-solid, silent ascent systems that serve as signature architectural centerpieces. The firm emphasizes direct professional design collaboration, rigorous safety checks, and a commitment to lasting quality.

old_description: Founded by siblings Kiffin and Kelly Ward, the company is committed to domestic manufacturing and building long-term partnerships by delivering high-quality, made-in-USA parts with unmatched flexibility.
about:
Ward's Manufacturing operates from Warren, Rhode Island, where siblings Kiffin and Kelly Ward founded the company in 2022. The woman-owned, millennial-owned business began after the pair experienced firsthand the difficulties of sourcing reliable domestic metal fabrication and decided to fill that gap themselves, drawing on a family legacy of tradespeople and a commitment to U.S.-based production.

The shop provides custom metal fabrication including fiber laser cutting, CNC press brake bending, machining, finishing, and product design. Its equipment includes a 3 kW fiber optic laser with a 5-by-10-foot bed capable of cutting mild steel up to 3/4 inch, stainless up to 3/8 inch, and aluminum up to 5/16 inch, plus a 190-ton CNC press brake that bends parts up to 10 feet long. In-house finishing covers #4 brushed, vibratory tumbling, glass bead blasting, and orbital sanding, while value-added services range from powder coating and anodizing to welding, assembly, and heat treating. The company reports a 99% quality rate and handles orders from single prototypes to production runs of tens of thousands of units with no minimum order quantity.

Ward's serves customers across aerospace and defense, marine, robotics and automation, renewable energy (solar frames, wind turbine components), medical devices, electronics enclosures, and industrial equipment. Concrete examples include aircraft components, marine-grade corrosion-resistant parts, robotic sensor components, solar panel frames, wind energy parts, medical-grade metal parts, and electronic enclosures and brackets. The company has shipped to 43 U.S. states and four Canadian provinces.

The founders started the business to address the lack of responsive, high-quality domestic fabrication options they encountered as buyers. They emphasize short lead times — including 24- to 48-hour expedited delivery — flexible scheduling, responsive communication, and the supply-chain security of all-U.S. production. Woman-owned (WBE-certified) and Green Manufacturer certifications help clients meet supplier diversity and sustainability goals.

Its core capabilities include custom weaving of high-strength polyester, nylon, and polypropylene fibers; textile lamination; custom adhesive formulation using RFL and isocyanate chemistries; and performance coating. A noted partnership with European manufacturer Bohle produced the TurtleSkin High Density Guard material used in Schwalbe tires such as the Ultremo, Marathon Supreme, and DD Racing Ralph lines. Warwick emphasizes a cooperative development philosophy that combines engineering and manufacturing under one roof. It states that designing with manufacturing in mind yields a seamless development strategy with shorter production times. The firm highlights its integrated development and manufacturing capabilities as a unique advantage in the protective textiles industry, backed by ISO 9001:2015 certification.

about:
Wayne Mills has operated in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania since 1910. The family-owned business, now in its fifth generation, began weaving twill tapes and light webbings when steam was coal-fired and yarn arrived by horse-drawn wagon.

Today the company runs a 150,000-square-foot complex of nine buildings on four acres in the city's historic Germantown district. More than 60 employees—many with decades of tenure—operate warping and weaving machines, a high-speed bleaching range, a computer-controlled Mageba continuous dye line, and 16 skein dyeing machines. The facility also houses custom coating, reflective lamination, and cutting/packaging lines. Stock items such as cotton tapes (styles 6210, 5541, 5526, 4214, 5533) ship quickly, while custom orders are fulfilled with the same attention to detail.

The narrow fabrics serve apparel, bag and strap makers, military-specification programs, and safety applications requiring reflective lamination. Customers include Analog Watch Company and public-sector buyers such as the Philadelphia Commerce Department.

Wayne Mills differentiates itself with a 15-pound minimum for custom dye lots—far below the industry's typical 500- to 1,000-pound threshold—and an in-house quality lab that tests break strength, elongation, wash fastness, and adhesive performance. Environmental awards recognize its wastewater treatment, and the firm emphasizes U.S. manufacturing.

about:
West Automotive Products was founded in 1983 in Canby, Oregon, by Don West, a mechanic, entrepreneur, and inventor. West began experimenting with wooden dowels to solve the difficulty of aligning the disc and flywheel during manual transmission clutch replacement, eventually developing a custom plastic injection molding process that became the foundation of the company.

The company designs, fabricates, and delivers clutch alignment tools used in aftermarket clutch kits for thousands of engine types, producing more than 200 unique tools via injection molding. Its Oregon facility handles all design and manufacturing in-house without outsourcing, and also produces drink holders, quick disconnect tools, transmission plugs, seal installers, and timing chain tools. The injection molding process uses 100 percent post-industrial material, and byproducts are re-fabricated to eliminate industrial waste.

West Automotive serves the automotive aftermarket, heavy-duty trucking, and agricultural equipment sectors across North America, Central America, and overseas markets. Its customers include manufacturers of aftermarket clutch kits who rely on the company’s 100 percent fill rates and on-time delivery to meet their own production schedules. The firm works directly with clients’ R&D departments to develop custom alignment tools for new and existing applications.

Don West’s original goal was to bring more precision to clutch replacement, a mission that still drives the company’s quality guarantee — offering full exchange or refund if products do not meet requirements — and its commitment to streamlined, waste-free manufacturing.

name: Western Washington Sheet Metal
old_description: Angela joined the Western Washington Sheet Metal JATC in 2017 after transferring from the SM JATC in Las Vegas, where she had been employed since 2008. Her introduction to the sheet metal industry came through a friend who worked at the JATC and recommended it as a promising career path.
about:
Established in 2008, the Western Washington Sheet Metal Joint Apprenticeship Training Committee (JATC) operates as a non-profit labor-management partnership headquartered in Everett, Washington, with a second campus in DuPont. The committee was formed by the Sheet Metal Air, Rail and Transportation Workers (SMART) Local 66 and the Sheet Metal and Air Conditioning Contractors' Association (SMACNA) Western Washington to provide standardized apprenticeship training for the region's sheet metal industry. While union apprenticeship in the trade dates back over a century, the modern JATC structure has been in place since 1973.

The JATC delivers tuition-free apprenticeship programs in four core disciplines: sheet metal fabrication and installation, testing adjusting and balancing (TAB), HVAC service, and residential sheet metal. Training combines on-the-job placement with one of 72 signatory contractors—ranging from small shops to large mechanical firms such as MacDonald-Miller, Hermanson Company, and McKinstry—with classroom and lab instruction at the two campuses. The center employs 12 full-time staff, including seven instructors with a combined 210 years of industry experience, and typically enrolls roughly 500 apprentices, graduating about 98 journey-level workers annually.

Graduates enter the commercial construction, HVAC, and building trades sectors, with notable project experience in healthcare facilities, smoke control systems, and energy-efficient heat pump installations recognized by the U.S. Department of Energy. The DuPont campus hosts the SMART Heroes program, which provides a direct entry pathway for active-duty military personnel and veterans. Apprentices earn competitive wages—starting at $70,520 annually with full benefits including retirement, medical, dental, and vision—while incurring zero student debt and receiving credit toward an associate degree.

The JATC's governing board comprises six labor trustees and six management trustees, ensuring curriculum aligns with contractor needs. Instructors bring field expertise from major projects for clients such as Microsoft, SpaceX, Costco, and regional healthcare systems, and hold certifications including WABO welding, TABB, and NEMI/ICB credentials. The program's mission centers on producing a highly skilled, competitive workforce through joint labor-management collaboration.

about:
Zen By Design was established in 2001 in Scottsdale, Arizona, as a family-run venture dedicated to crafting meditation furniture. The company began with the intention of bringing more comfort and harmony to meditation practice, hand-building each piece in its Scottsdale workshop.

The company produces a line of meditation chairs—including the Tantra Chair, Anahata, Rama, Samurai, and the portable Zenfu zafu—along with meditation candles. Every chair is handcrafted from eco-friendly materials; artisans individually select each piece of wood and fabric, and the ergonomic design provides a gentle sacral tilt and back support for extended sitting. Over more than two decades, the workshop has supplied tens of thousands of meditators worldwide.

Customers range from individual practitioners to ashrams and meditation centers across nearly every nation. Notable clients have included Dr. Deepak Chopra, Dr. Andrew Weil, The Oprah Winfrey Show, Jack Canfield, and His Holiness the Dalai Lama. The company serves both newcomers to meditation and lifelong practitioners seeking relief from physical discomfort during practice.

Zen By Design emphasizes that its furniture is made in the USA with no expense spared for excellence, and it maintains a 100 percent customer-satisfaction record. The team is available seven days a week, year-round, and the founders say they are motivated by the desire to create the finest products at a fair price, believing that furniture created with love can be felt and enjoyed for a lifetime.

The firm also supplies optical interconnects for AI data centers and LiDAR solutions for autonomous vehicles.

The company positions itself as a "Photonics Powerhouse," differentiating through its combination of light emission, detection, and intelligence — what it calls Digital Photonics. Its mission emphasizes pioneering lighting and sensing technologies that make the world safer, smarter, and more sustainable, backed by a culture of innovation, trust, and speed.

about:
Based in Great Falls, Montana, 406 Processing & Taxidermy operates as a locally owned whole-animal butchery.

The facility provides year-round processing services for both wild game and livestock. During hunting season, the shop handles deer, elk, and antelope, while its livestock program offers on-ranch slaughtering—teams travel to the ranch to harvest animals and transport them back for cutting, wrapping, and specialty meat production. The taxidermy side produces European skull mounts using a beetle-cleaning method that preserves delicate bone structure, as well as full taxidermy mounts crafted by award-winning taxidermist Brad Lencioni.

The company emphasizes that every carcass is tracked so clients receive meat from their own animal, a guarantee highlighted on its about page.

Differentiators cited by the company include the guarantee of meat identity, the convenience of on-ranch slaughter, the beetle-based European mount process that avoids bone shrinkage, and the reputation of its taxidermists for trophy-quality work. Lencioni frames the business as a family-oriented operation built on trust and personal pride in each step from field to table.

old_description: Here is a great explanation from Wikipedia when searching "OEM": "An Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) is a company that produces parts and equipment that may be marketed by another manufacturer. For example, if Acme Manufacturing Co. makes power cords that are used on IBM computers, Acme is an OEM. The term is also used in several other ways, which causes ambiguity. It sometimes means the maker of a system that includes other companies' subsystems, an end-product producer, an automotive part that is manufactured by the same company that produced the original part used in the automobile's assembly, or a value-added reseller." "When referring to auto parts, OEM refers to the manufacturer of the original equipment, that is, the parts assembled and installed during the construction of a new vehicle. In contrast, aftermarket parts are those made by companies other than the OEM, which might be installed as replacements after the car comes out of the factory. For example, if Ford used Autolite spark plugs, Exide batteries, Bosch fuel injectors, and Ford's own engine blocks and heads when building a car, then car restorers and collectors consider those to be the OEM parts. Other-brand parts would be considered aftermarket, such as Champion spark plugs, DieHard batteries, Kinsler fuel injectors, and BMP engine blocks and heads. Many auto parts manufacturers sell parts through multiple channels, for example to car makers for installation during new-vehicle construction, to car makers for resale as automaker-branded replacement parts, and through general merchandising supply chains. Any given brand of part can be OE on some vehicle models and aftermarket on others".

about:
Altek Electronics Inc., now operating as a Cyient DLM company, is headquartered in Torrington, Connecticut. The business was founded in 1972 by Stephen Altschuler, an electrical engineer with degrees from the University of Connecticut and Yale University. Altschuler previously held leadership roles at Computer Dynamics and Adage Inc. before establishing Altek to serve the electronics assembly market.

The firm provides full-service electronics manufacturing, including surface-mount and through-hole PCB assembly, BGA placement, selective and wave soldering, wire and cable harness fabrication, conformal coating, and box-build system integration. Operations are supported by equipment such as the ERSA Versaflow 3/66 selective soldering system, a PVA6000 conformal coating machine with IR2000 curing oven, and automated component counting and barcode traceability systems. The facility employs more than 130 people and handles programs ranging from prototype runs to full-rate production.

Altek serves original equipment manufacturers in the medical, aerospace, defense, telecommunications, industrial/commercial, and transportation sectors. The company was an early adopter of AS9100, achieving “C” level certification and later upgrading to the “D” revision in April 2017. Its quality system is also certified to ISO 9001, ISO 13485 for medical devices, and IATF 16949 for automotive, and it maintains ITAR registration for defense-related work.

Altschuler’s founding philosophy centered on customer satisfaction, on-time bill payment, and a reputation for reliability. The company states it is dedicated to offering the highest quality electronics at the most competitive price without compromising its core beliefs, a principle that has guided its growth over five decades.

about:
Earthfirst Films, a division of Aluf Plastics, is headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, with additional manufacturing sites in Orangeburg, New York, and Sulphur Springs, Texas. The business traces its roots to 1949 when Joe Tatem founded Plastic Suppliers as a privately held corporation in Blackwood, New Jersey. In 2025 the Earthfirst Films brand was acquired by API, continuing its focus on sustainable packaging.

The company manufactures compostable sealant films, barrier sealant films, and laminates using blown film extrusion and cast-and-tenter extrusion technologies. Its Columbus campus operates a blown film facility and a tenter film facility supported by an on-site laboratory equipped with two lab extruders for tensile, barrier, FTIR, and microscopy testing. Capabilities include lamination, high-speed slitting, converting, and fast prototyping with small-batch production runs.

Earthfirst Films serves the food, beverage, medical, personal care, office, industrial, and broader consumer packaged goods (CPG) sectors. Its films are used in applications such as flow wrap, shrink sleeve decoration, and print web structures, targeting brands that require certified home-compostable or industrial-compostable packaging solutions.

The company states its mission is to create sustainable solutions through open collaboration. It highlights a legacy of over 20 years in biopolymer film extrusion, holding several patents on compostable sealant films, and offering materials beyond PLA, including PHA and other biobased polymers. The 2019 SQF certification for its blown film facility underscores a commitment to food-grade packaging standards.

about:
Applied Molding Technologies, LLC was founded in 2006 in Frederic, Wisconsin.

The shop provides thermoplastic injection molding on all-electric presses ranging from 55 to 850 tons of clamp force, and thermoset compression, transfer, and injection molding on presses from 150 to 300 tons. It also offers value-added mechanical assembly including heat-staking, ultrasonic inserts, sub-assemblies, kitting, and ship-direct packaging. Production runs 24/7/365 on a four-shift rotation designed to minimize start-up and shut-down scrap. Tooling is sourced both domestically and off-shore, with in-house maintenance and repair.

Applied Molding serves a global customer base with varying technical, regulatory, and commercial requirements. Its thermoset capabilities target electrical and dielectric components as well as large or thick-section parts, while its thermoplastic work spans commodity and engineering-grade resins. The company scales engineering, quality, and program-management support to each customer's needs.

The business was built on the premise that domestic manufacturing could compete through a fundamentally different operating model rather than low-wage competition. Its founders designed the company for efficiency, customization, and adaptability—retaining core capabilities in-house while partnering for ancillary functions, and continuously revisiting processes through structured improvement.

old_description: At Arizona Woodworks we employ the highest quality craftsman and the best materials to create the custom built cabinets, mantles, furniture, and commercial woodwork. A Prescott cabinet and woodworker for more than 30 years, we have the experience to design and build beautiful wood cabinetry and furniture   to fit any home or commercial application. …
about:
Arizona Woodworks operates from Prescott, Arizona, where it has been a cabinet and woodworking presence for over three decades.

The shop produces custom built cabinets, mantles, heirloom furniture, commercial woodwork, and millwork. It emphasizes the use of skilled craftsmen and a range of wood species and finishes to meet both residential and commercial project requirements.

Customers include homeowners seeking one-of-a-kind furniture pieces and businesses needing commercial millwork. A 2019 testimonial from Rich and Pam Arnold notes the company delivered everything from garage shelving to artistic focal-point furniture, highlighting its ability to handle varied scales and design needs.

name: Arkansas Glass Container Corporation
old_description: Arkansas Glass Container Corporation, located in Jonesboro, Arkansas, has been on the same property since 1948. Originally built to produce minnow-roach bait traps, a change in ownership and the company name in the mid-1950s resulted in a shift to food-grade containers -- a product that we still produce today. Proud to be American owned, Arkansas Glass Container Corporation, makes glass containers ranging from 8 ounces to one-gallon. We also offer a family of patented designed containers called the Stout, used for sauces, beverages or dressings.
about:
Arkansas Glass Container Corporation has operated from the same property in Jonesboro, Arkansas since 1948. The facility was originally built to produce minnow-roach bait traps; a change in ownership and company name in the mid-1950s redirected production to food-grade glass containers, a line that continues today. The company describes itself as American owned.

The company manufactures clear glass containers for the food and beverage industries, with capacities from 8 ounces to one gallon. Its product line includes a patented family of containers branded as Stout, designed for sauces, beverages, and dressings. The catalog lists numerous stock items identified by part numbers such as A1168-00 and A0032-12, though total SKU count, facility square footage, and employee headcount are not disclosed.

Arkansas Glass Container serves the food and beverage industries, supplying containers for products such as sauces, beverages, and dressings. No specific customer names or end-market segments beyond those categories are provided.

The company emphasizes its American ownership and its patented Stout container line as distinguishing features. The original pivot from bait traps to food-grade containers in the 1950s established its current market focus.
